As a result, their mass retention rate increased by 2.8-fold after one week of open storage and their mass loss rate is reduced by 3.4-fold after 24 hours of vigorous vibration compared with regular LOHCs.
items.authors: Xiaoying Lu, Yushuai Huang, Peng Peng, Libin Tian, Xiaokang Chen, Ziqing Mao

items.title: A Hidden Acid–Base Ion Pair Scaffolds Organic-Rich Atmospheric Nucleation
items.abstract: New particle formation is widely observed in organic-rich atmospheric environments where sulfuric acid and basic vapors appear scarce, yet what initiates nucleation and what role trace inorganic acid–base species play remain unclear. Guided by laboratory experiments and field observations, we resolve this ambiguity with a bottom-up framework bridging molecular energetics and nucleation kinetics, tracking nucleation from molecular origin to measurable formation rates. We uncover a hidden pathway in which a multifunctional oxygenated organic molecule (OOM) hydrogen-bonds simultaneously to sulfuric acid and ammonia, inducing proton transfer and stabilizing a charge-separated HSO 4 - –NH 4 + ion pair. This ion pair forms a localized electrostatic scaffold that recruits additional OOMs into a charge-assisted hydrogen-bond network, yielding stable embryonic clusters. Remarkably, a single ion pair unlocks this mechanism, indicating that even trace inorganic species can be indispensable nucleation triggers. Operating across diverse biogenic and anthropogenic OOM systems, ion-pair-scaffolded nucleation may be ubiquitous in the atmosphere.
items.authors: Huan Yang, Markku Kulmala, Renyi Zhang, Yafang Cheng

items.title: From Computational Chemistry to Generative Models: A Survey of AI-Driven Small-Molecule Drug Discovery
items.abstract: Small-molecule drug discovery requires navigating enormous chemical space to identify candidates that are simultaneously potent, selective, synthetically accessible, and acceptable across pharmacokinetic and safety profiles; modern generative AI extends a long computational medicinal chemistry lineage that began with QSAR, pharmacophore modeling, and early structure-based de novo design. This survey focuses primarily on developments from 2017 to 2025, with the literature updated through 31 January 2026. Using a medicinal-chemistry lens, it first establishes the shared machinery of the field: molecular representations such as SMILES, SELFIES, graphs, fingerprints, three-dimensional coordinates, voxels, and latent vectors; commonly used datasets and benchmarks; and graph neural network encoders, including message-passing, directional, and equivariant architectures. We compare five principal generative mechanisms—autoregressive models, variational autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, normalizing flows, and diffusion models—together with reinforcement learning as a major goal-directed optimization framework. Across these approaches, we show that current methods offer complementary rather than interchangeable trade-offs, and we highlight recurring challenges, including validity versus synthesizability, limited prospective experimental validation, mode collapse and diversity loss, stereochemical and physical realism in three-dimensional design, computational cost, data scarcity, and the emerging convergence toward scaffold-conditioned generation, hybrid architectures, developability-aware optimization, and molecular foundation models.
items.authors: Houman Kazemzadeh, Kiarash Mokhtari, Nazanin Mirzaei, Seyed Reza Tavakoli, Ali Reza Keivanimehr, Shayan Majidifar

items.title: Coordinate bonding, cluster delocalization and topological criticality in a cyclic trimeric beryllium–dinitrogen complex
items.abstract: Fixation and coordination of molecular dinitrogen (N2) by main-group clusters offer fundamental insight into non-classical multi-centre bonding and light-metal activation pathways. Here we report a combined density-functional and ab initio study of the cyclic cluster Be3(N2)3. Geometry optimization and frequency analysis establish a stable, closed-shell Cs-symmetric trimer containing an isosceles triangular Be3 metal core coordinated end-on by three terminal N2 ligands. Energy decomposition analysis coupled with natural orbitals for chemical valence (ETS-NOCV) shows that the Be3⋯(N2)3 interaction is dominated by orbital contributions (≈60 % of attractive forces), supplemented by electrostatic attraction that together overcome Pauli repulsion. Quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM) identifies two non-nuclear attractors along the apical–basal Be–Be edges, while electron localization function (ELF) and localized orbital locator (LOL) basin analyses reveal a distinct heart-shaped trisynaptic valence basin V(Be,Be,Be) populated by ≈1.8–2.0 electrons. These topological signatures establish multi-centre σ-aromatic delocalization as the structural foundation of the central metallacycle and demonstrate that light alkaline-earth elements can support non-classical N2 coordination frameworks.
items.authors: D K Jha, M Pathak, Dhananjay Kumar Jha

items.title: Nanothermodynamic Generalization of the Young–Laplace and Young Equations for Sessile Droplets with Line Effects
items.abstract: Thermodynamic investigations of wetting phenomena require that we handle the nanoscale. By combining Hill’s small-system thermodynamics with a Gibbsian composite-system description, we formulate the equilibrium thermodynamics of a sessile nanodroplet. We consider a one-component liquid droplet resting on an ideal, flat, inert solid substrate and in contact with reservoirs that fix the temperature and chemical potential. Finite-size effects are retained in the liquid bulk phase, the liquid–vapor interface, and the three-phase contact line, while the solid–vapor and solid–liquid interfaces are assumed to follow regular thermodynamics and treated macroscopically. The distinction between integral and differential pressure, surface tension, and line tension is used to derive nanothermodynamic generalizations of the Young–Laplace and Young equations. The resulting equations account for the size-and shape dependence of the finite thermodynamic contributions and recover the classical equilibrium equations in the macroscopic limit.
items.authors: Vitor H. C. Cunha, Signe Kjelstrup, Dick Bedeaux, Vitor Heitor Cardoso Cunha

items.title: Interfacial Position Governs the Dual Functionality of Carbazole Layers in Cu2O Photocathodes
items.abstract: Organic-inorganic hybrid photoelectrodes offer a promising strategy to improve charge separation in photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems, yet the influence of the spatial position of ultrathin organic interlayers remains poorly understood. Herein, we integrate electropolymerized carbazole-based conjugated porous polymers (CPPs) into Cu2O photocathodes by positioning the polymer either beneath or on top of the semiconductor. Both hybrid architectures exhibit en-hanced PEC performance compared with bare Cu2O, with the highest photocur-rent achieved when the polymer is deposited as an ultrathin overlayer. A combi-nation of electrochemical impedance spectroscopy together with femtosecond and nanosecond transient absorption spectroscopy reveals that the carbazole interlayer performs two distinct functions depending on its position within the hybrid architecture. When located beneath Cu2O, the polymer primarily facili-tates directional hole extraction and charge separation. In contrast, when depos-ited on top of Cu2O, the ultrathin polymer predominantly passivates surface defects, suppressing interfacial recombination and extending charge-carrier life-times while preserving efficient interfacial charge transfer. The triscarbazole-based polymer consistently exhibits slightly improved charge-transport proper-ties compared with its biscarbazole analogue. These findings demonstrate that the functionality of ultrathin organic interlayers is governed not only by their molecular structure but also by their spatial position within hybrid photoelec-trodes. More broadly, this work establishes interfacial positioning as a simple yet powerful design principle for engineering charge-carrier dynamics in organic-inorganic photoelectrochemical systemsgoes here.
items.authors: Alejandro García-Eguizábal, Miguel Garcí­a-Tecedor, Miguel Gomez-Mendoza, Freddy Oropeza, Soranyel Gonzalez-Carrero, James R. Durrant

items.title: Efficiency and Accessibility Are Not Enough: Chemical-Validity Filtering in High-Throughput Screening of Organic Photovoltaic Materials
items.abstract: Descriptor-based screening for organic photovoltaics ranks molecules on computed properties such as frontier-orbital energies and synthetic accessibility, but such descriptors do not test whether a highly ranked molecule is a chemically sensible material. We screened 17,458 molecules from the PubChemQC database using PCESAScore—Scharber-model efficiency minus the RDKit synthetic-accessibility score—and examined what the metric actually returns. Seven molecules cross the viability threshold, but three are not organic semiconductors (molecular oxygen, a magnesium carbonate salt, a quinhydrone cocrystal) and three more carry reactive groups (two azides, one nitroso). A transparent chemicalvalidity filter and a reactive-group screen reduce the viable set from seven to four to a single stable candidate. The top-ranked molecule, an azidotriazine, reaches a 36.1% nominal efficiency—above the Scharber model’s single-junction ceiling—from a 0.91 eV gap, and carries a 9.26 D dipole and a negative computed reorganization energy: signatures of an unusable material, not a lead. Across the dataset, heteroatom composition correlates only weakly with orbital energies (|r| ≤ 0.34), so no simple design rule holds. Descriptor-based materials screens require an explicit chemical-validity and stability gate; the gap between the pre-and post-gate viable sets is a result in itself.
items.authors: Patrick Sorrel Mvoto Kongo, Steve Cabrel Teguia Kouam, Jean-Pierre TCHAPET NJAFA, Serge Guy Nana Engo

items.title: Stannylene Ambiphilicity Enables Formation of a Trimetallic Complex
items.abstract: Low-valent heavier group 14 tetrylenes combine a stereochemically active lone pair with a vacant p-orbital at a single centre, resulting in a unique ambiphilic reactivity profile. However, exploiting these donor–acceptor properties to construct transition-metal complexes featuring bridging tetrylene units remains largely unexplored. Here we report a flexible pincer ligand in which an N,O,N pocket stabilises the monomeric stannylene [(PNONP)Sn] (Sn1) that itself presents a P,Sn,P pocket for nickel coordination and can be employed, either stepwise or in one pot, to afford the isolable NHC-stabilised tin–nickel heterobimetallics [(PNONP)SnNi(NHC)] Sn4a,b (NHC = N-heterocyclic carbene). Reaction of Sn4a with W(CO)6, envisaged as a simple test electrophile for the tin-centred lone pair, instead proceeds via unanticipated NHC-to-CO exchange and the resulting NHC-free tin–nickel-carbonyl fragment self-associates to give the dimeric complex [(PNONP)SnNi(CO)]2 (Sn5). Treatment of Sn4a with [(p-cymene)Ru(Cl)2]2 affords the target heterotrimetallic Ni–Sn–Ru complex [(PNONP)Sn{Ru(Cl)2(p-cyemene)}Ni(IiPr2Me2)] (Sn6), in which tin bridges the metal centres in a genuinely push–pull fashion, representing the first structurally authentification of such a bonding mode for a heavy tetrylene.
items.authors: Jonathan Kieselbach, Christopher Golz, Jasmin Alsadi, Josh Abbenseth, Malte Fischer

items.title: Photocatalytic synthesis of functionalized polymers on primary human T cells
items.abstract: Polymers can be designed to impart new functions to the surfaces of tissues and cells, making them valuable tools for bioengineering applications. Existing grafting-to methods suffer from low polymer grafting efficiencies – due in part to challenging-to-control lipid anchoring strategies. One solution to these limitations is to adopt a grafting-from approach, where polymers are synthesized at defined initiation sites on the cell surface. Previous studies have highlighted the value of cytocompatible photocatalyzed grafting-from polymer chemistries or site-specific covalent anchoring of initiation sites; however, unification of these features remains unexplored. Further, no grafting-from technologies have been applied to surface engineering of primary human cells. To address this gap, we have combined Photo-Induced Electron-Transfer Reversible Addition-Fragmentation Chain-Transfer (PET-RAFT) chemistry with site selective surface anchoring of a custom traceable oligomeric polymer initiation site. We show that our approach enabled efficient grafting-from chain extension of functionally diverse polymers anchored on cell surface carbohydrates (glycans). The approach was compatible with both an immortalized human cell line and primary human immune cells (T cells). This technology provides a framework for site-selective modification of primary cell surfaces without genetic manipulation.
items.authors: Olivia Mann-Delany, Fauzia N. Izzati, Richard Fuku, Jon Babi, Qingyu Shi, Vanessa Affe

items.title: Toward Property-Directed Catalytic Skeletal Editing of Functional Organic Materials
items.abstract: Late-stage skeletal editing has emerged as a useful strategy in synthetic and medicinal chemistry for altering molecular frameworks by atom insertion, deletion, replacement, or bond reorganization. Functional organic molecules and materials are commonly optimized through peripheral substitution and de novo framework construction. Direct modification of an existing skeleton provides a complementary means of tuning electronic structure, molecular shape, chirality, packing, and processability. Herein we examine catalytic skeletal editing with an emphasis on functional organic materials, specifically π-conjugated molecules, dyes, polymers, and covalent frameworks. Representative examples are evaluated in terms of catalytic status and experimentally demonstrated properties. Key requirements for broader application include site selectivity, element transfer, catalyst compatibility, and control of editing extent in extended materials. The emerging opportunity is to move skeletal editing from reaction-centered diversification toward catalyst-controlled, property-directed modification.
items.authors: Taichi Koike, Sajan Pradhan, Kenichiro Itami

items.title: Extended QM/Me: Quantum-Mechanical Explicit Solvation at Solid–Liquid Interfaces
items.abstract: We extend the subtractive QM/Me embedding scheme from vacuum to liquid environments: the adsorbate and explicit solvent are treated by a periodic quantum-mechanical layer above a classical metal bath, avoiding the need for metal–solvent interaction parameters. For methoxy on Pt(111) in water (3070 quantum atoms), the performance of three tight-binding Hamiltonians for adiabatic solvation shifts is assessed. The embedding provides analytic energy gradients and substantially reduced computational cost compared to a fully quantum-mechanical model.
items.authors: You Lu, Thomas W. Keal

items.title: Single-particle FRET reveals ligand configurations on colloidal perovskite quantum dots
items.abstract: The functionality of colloidal quantum dots (QDs), whether in fundamental studies, optoelectronics, or emerging quantum technologies, critically depends on their surface chemistry, with organic ligands influencing nearly every aspect of their behavior. Whereas the inorganic core can be comprehensively characterized at atomic resolution, ligands remain dibicult to probe owing to their low atomic contrast and soft, disordered structure. Here, we empower single-particle photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy to resolve ligand conformations at sub-nanometer resolution. Tagging ligand tails with organic dyes enables measuring their distance from the QD via Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET). Single-particle, single-molecule FRET experiments performed on lead halide perovskite QDs reveal nanometer-scale variations in dye-surface distances, both within individual particles (0.81 ± 0.22 nm on average) and between QDs with varied ligand chemistries (from 0.25 nm to 1.02 nm). Supported by atomistic modelling, our experiments tie variations in the local ligand environment to this conformational diversity. A powerful yet accessible spectroscopic method for interrogating the complex surface chemistry of QDs is highly relevant to QD-based optoelectronics, quantum applications, and photocatalysis.
items.authors: Leon G. Feld, Oleksandr Kolomiiets, Noah Shahin, Sebastian Sabisch, Gabriele Rainò, Maksym V. Kovalenko

items.title: Vicinal Chlorination of Dehydrogenated Polyethylene Toward Applications of Waste Polyolefins
items.abstract: Post-polymerization vicinal chlorination of unsaturated polyolefins provides access to linear poly(ethylene-co-1,2-dichloroethylene) polymers that are inaccessible through conventional polymerization or post-polymerization routes. Herein, Cl 2 (g), generated in situ from N-chlorosuccinimide (NCS) and hydrochloric acid (HCl), was used to selectively convert alkene sites in polycyclooctene (PCOE)-derived polyolefins into vicinal chloride subunits. Partial hydrogenation of PCOE afforded substrates containing 4–25 mol% residual C=C, which upon chlorination, yielded polymers with controlled levels and distributions of vicinal chlorides along a linear polyethylene backbone. Incorporation of chlorides into the PCOE-derived polymers disrupts crystal formation and reduces the glass transition and melting temperatures. For the 25 mol% vicinal chloride, the polymer affords precise placement of chlorides along the polymer backbone and transforms the orthorhombic crystal structure, typical of polyethylene (PE), to a triclinic crystal structure, suggesting the incorporation of Cl atoms to the crystallites. This method was further extended to dehydrogenated post-consumer HDPE from milk jugs, affording vicinal chlorinated polyethylene containing ~ 1.1 mol% vicinal Cl, while maintaining the original polymer chain architecture and molecular weight. These results establish vicinal chlorination of unsaturated PE as a strategy for tuning polymer properties and provide a platform for upcycling PEs into value-added functional materials.
items.authors: Pedro M. Jimenez Antenucci, Tingfeng Chen, Hoda Shokrollahzadeh Behbahani, Huapei Qiu, Lucia Lavelle, Emily Sidlow

items.title: Cooperative Inorganic-Organic Binding Sites in Zeolite Adsorbents Enhance CO 2 Capture and Water Resistance
items.abstract: Optimization of amine-based adsorbents for carbon capture technologies requires next-generation materials capable of handling a broad range of operating conditions with high amine efficiency. The current disadvantages of liquid amine absorbents motivate the design of porous solid analogues as alternatives. Here we present a bifunctional zeolite comprised of silanol defects and grafted amines that cooperatively bind CO 2 with 97% amine efficiency. We use a borosilicate beta zeolite as a parent material and generate a high density of silanol defects through facile post-synthesis demetalation, followed by amine functionalization. Spectroscopic techniques and density functional theory calculations confirm that silylpropylcarbamate species enhance CO 2 binding through an activated process with optimal performance at 100℃, which markedly reduces the temperature swing for regeneration without loss in performance after multiple cycles. Systematic analysis of carbon capture performance reveals that CO 2 sorption capacity doubles when shifting from high to low temperature, and is positively influenced by humidity.
items.authors: Debasmita Halder, Mingze Zheng, Hardik K. Balsaraf, Taimin Yang, Zachariah J. Berkson, Brandon C. Bukowski

items.title: Benzimidazole Modification of DNA Aptamers for Ultra Responsive Protein-Induced Fluorescence Enhancement
items.abstract: Post-SELEX incorporation of environmentally responsive fluorescent nucleobase surrogates provides a powerful strategy for converting DNA aptamers into protein aptasensors, yet achieving large protein-induced fluorescence enhancement (PIFE) while preserving target affinity remains a major challenge.Here, we introduce a photobasic 4-(1H-benzo[d]imidazol-2-yl)-N,N-dimethylaniline (AnIm) nucleobase surrogate that enables ultraresponsive PIFE through site-specific incorporation into DNA aptamers.As a model system, AnIm was incorporated into two thrombin-binding aptamers that recognize distinct protein exosites: the 15-mer TBA15 and the 27-mer HD22.The modified aptamers retained high thrombin affinity (Kd = 85-167 nM).Within HD22, site-dependent fluorescence enhancements of 70-108-fold (Irel) were observed, affording a limit of detection (LOD) of 280 pM in PBS and 3.8 nM in 5% human serum.To our knowledge, this >100-fold fluorescence turn-on represents the largest PIFE response reported for a fluorescent nucleobase surrogate.Spectroscopic studies reveal that the exceptional sensitivity arises from a protein-induced pKa shift coupled with suppression of a twisted intramolecular charge-transfer (TICT) state.Protein binding shifts AnIm from its protonated (NH⁺) ground-state toward the neutral (N) form, reducing background fluorescence, while excited-state protonation generates a fluorescent molecular rotor whose emission is enhanced within the rigid protein microenvironment.These findings establish photobasic nucleobase surrogates as a general strategy for post-SELEX fluorescent aptamer engineering for ultra-responsive PIFE-based biosensing.
items.authors: Matteo Pavlovic, Austin Pounder, Naomi Varnovitski, Stacey D. Wetmore, Richard A. Manderville

items.title: Spacing Over Sequence: Design Considerations for Polystyrene-binding Polypeptides
items.abstract: Plastic-binding polypeptides have emerging applications in biosensor design, materials functionalization, and nanoplastic capture, and the rational design of new sequences requires the development of structural and sequence-based design principles. Here, we demonstrate a computational workflow combining atomistic molecular dynamics simulations and enhanced sampling to evaluate polypeptide binding to polystyrene, a common commodity plastic. We investigate two candidate sequences previously proposed as polystyrene binders, both enriched in either aromatic or cationic residues expected to interact with polystyrene's aromatic rings. We find that the two sequences bind stably through apparent π-stacking and cation-π interactions. These binding modalities rely on proper residue spacing; not all cationic residues on a polypeptide bind unless separated by linking residues as demonstrated by our “arginine claw” motif. We also determine that the presence of the polypeptide does shield the polystyrene from contacts with solvent, though it does not promote further self-collapse of the oligomer. Our analysis demonstrates how sequence composition coupled with sequence orientation enables multiple binding modalities, determining motifs such as the “arginine claw” and aromatic ring distribution that can be leveraged in future polypeptide design.
items.authors: Mansi Gokani, Brianna Z. Fea, Ashley Z. Guo

items.title: Which state are you converging? A spin audit of sample-based quantum diagonalization benchmarks on iron–sulfur clusters
items.abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD/QSCI) diagonalizes the Hamiltonian classically in determinant subspaces selected from quantum-circuit samples. Its iron–sulfur demonstrations underpin claims of utility-scale quantum chemistry, and a recent critique disputes them at matched subspace dimension. Both sides compare energies; neither reports which spin state was computed. Our spin audit uses the exact determinant-space ⟨S²⟩, the invariant spectrum of the S² block over quasi-degenerate manifolds, and higher moments (⟨S⁴⟩ to ⟨S⁸⟩) bounding the spin-sector weights. We apply it to the public [2Fe-2S] and [4Fe-4S] benchmarks, IBM's released qiskit-addon-sqd pipeline and published hardware data. No audited execution returned the named singlet at competitive energy; for published states unavailable to direct audit, the energy-only records do not establish singlet identity. Under the audited HCI protocols, selected-CI growth approaches a spin-contaminated state (⟨S²⟩ ≈ 4.7 on [2Fe-2S]) whose samples keep the contamination. Spin-inversion completion leaves the energy and ⟨S²⟩ of these states unchanged. The released [2Fe-2S] hardware samples give no energy advantage over the released uniform-random control. A scalar mean does not identify these states: two audited arms share ⟨S²⟩ ≈ 2.00, but one is a triplet eigenstate (Var(S²) = 3×10⁻⁶) and the other a 2:1 singlet–quintet mixture whose third moment bounds its triplet weight below 10⁻⁴. At the largest published dimension (5.625×10⁷ determinants, reconstructed here from the released support), the lowest root, 170 mHa below the published energy, has ⟨S²⟩ = 1.3711, unchanged under an 18.6-fold residual tightening to 1.1% of the 0.285 mHa gap. Its first two moments, with Var(S²) = 6.9, exclude any decomposition confined to S ≤ 2. Near-singlet character appears only as a non-stationary superposition, because determinant selection does not commute with S². Energy-only benchmarks therefore do not establish convergence to the named state. We recommend reporting spin moments with every energy and controlling spin during selection.
items.authors: Tyler Vitale

items.title: Nitrile Geometry as an Architectural Code for Cu10 Nanocluster Metal–Organic Frameworks
items.abstract: Atomically precise nanoclusters offer molecularly defined metal architectures, yet their conversion into extended frameworks remains difficult because reticulation must impose long-range order without erasing the structural adaptability of the multinuclear node. Here, we show that nitrile geometry can function as an architectural code for Cu10 nanocluster metal–organic frameworks (NCMOFs). Rather than relying on conventional pyridyl donors, we employ sterically minimal aryl nitriles whose weaker donor character is coupled to sharply defined coordination vectors. Natural population analysis confirms that nitrile N atoms are substantially less electron-rich than representative pyridyl donors, establishing a distinct electronic regime for cluster reticulation. Using terephthalonitrile (TPN), isophthalonitrile (IPN), and 1,3,5-tricyanobenzene (TCB), we obtain four crystallographically distinct frameworks— Cu10TPN-1D, Cu10IPN-2D, Cu10IPN-1D, and Cu10TCB-2Dthrough diffusion-controlled assembly of a common Cu–thiolate precursor. Single-crystal structures reveal that the Cu–N interface remains comparatively constrained, while Cu···Cu, Cu–S, and especially Cu–O metrics reorganize to accommodate different linker vectors and lattice demands. Strikingly, the same 120° IPN linker yields either 1D or 2D connectivity depending on the crystallization medium, demonstrating that linker geometry defines an accessible connectivity landscape rather than a predetermined topology. These results establish a broader design principle for NCMOFs: directional information can be encoded in a weakly donating linker, while structural compliance is retained within the nanocluster node, enabling adaptive multinuclear units to translate molecular geometry into distinct reticular states.
items.authors: Ayumu Kondo, Riki Nakatani, Sreelakshmi K. S., Tsukasa Irie, Yunosuke Arai, Yuya Sugawara

items.title: Integrated CO2 removal and NH3 recovery from wastewater using a bidirectionally productive electrochemical pH swing
items.abstract: Electrochemical pH-swing processes based on proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) offer a promising route for selective chemical separation from aqueous media. Yet in all previous systems only one half of the pH swing performs a separation, while the reverse half is expended solely to regenerate the state of charge of the active electrode or electrolyte. Using a synthetic mimic of domestic wastewater as the input feed, we demonstrate a bidirectionally productive electrochemical pH-swing generated by a phenazine-carbon nanotube PCET-active composite electrode in an aqueous flow cell, in which both the acidifying and alkalizing half-cycles perform useful chemical separation. Electrode oxidation acidifies the wastewater to convert dissolved inorganic carbon into CO 2 (aq) for removal, whereas the subsequent reduction alkalizes the feed, converting NH 4 + to NH 3 (aq) for recovery using membrane stripping. An experimentally validated reaction-transport model establishes the pH-swing sequence as a key design parameter, with oxidation before reduction enabling integrated CO 2 removal and NH 3 recovery, whereas the opposite sequence prioritizes NH 3 recovery through near-complete NH 4 + -to-NH 3 conversion. The system achieved batchwise NH 3 recovery using the reduction–oxidation sequence over 31 cycles spanning 43 h, establishing operational stability over a duration not previously demonstrated for PCET-driven nutrient recovery. The oxidation–reduction sequence achieved average energetic costs of 219.9 kJ mol -1 CO 2 removed and 12.2 kWh kg -1 N recovered, with corresponding separation rates of 4.47 μmol CO 2 h -1 cm -2 and 5.33 g N m -2 day -1 , respectively. By making both directions of an electrochemical pH swing productive, this work reframes electrode regeneration as an opportunity for a second separation, and points toward wastewater treatment plants as distributed sites for combined nutrient recovery and carbon removal.
items.authors: Bin Yun, Orçun Dinçer, Marc-Antoni Goulet, David G. Kwabi

items.title: The Core Inverse of the Anti-Triangular Block Matrix over Rings
items.abstract: In this paper, we investigates the core inverse of the anti-triangular block matrix $M=\left( \begin{array}{cc} A amp;B\\ C amp;0 \end{array} \right)$ over a ring. We derive new explicit representations for the core inverse of $M$ under specific conditions. In particular, the EP property of $M$ involving two identical subblocks is investigated.
items.authors: Huanyin Chen

items.title: High-Flow Nasal Cannula in Adult Acute Care: Physiological Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, and Persistent Misconceptions
items.abstract: High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) oxygen therapy is widely used in emergency, inten-sive care, perioperative, and procedural settings, but it is often conceptually assimilated to non-invasive positive pressure ventilation (NIPPV). This interpretation is physio-logically misleading. HFNC is an open high-flow oxygen system whose main effects derive from dead-space washout, improved stability of inspired oxygen fraction (FiO₂), heated humidification, patient comfort, and only modest flow-dependent positive airway pressure. Its open interface also facilitates eating, drinking, speaking, and se-cretion clearance. Clinical evidence supports HFNC mainly in selected patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, where it may reduce intubation compared with conventional oxygen therapy. However, evidence is more heterogeneous in hypercap-nic respiratory failure, cardiogenic pulmonary edema, immunocompromised patients, obesity, and settings requiring substantial pressure support or ventilatory unloading. NIPPV or continuous positive airway pressure remain preferable when controlled positive pressure, alveolar recruitment, or ventilatory assistance are central to treat-ment. HFNC should therefore be regarded as optimized high-flow oxygen therapy rather than as “non-invasive ventilation through nasal prongs.” Recognizing this dis-tinction may improve patient selection, guide escalation, and avoid overinterpretation of its clinical effects.
items.authors: Daniele Orso, Francesco Meroi, Alessandro Brussa, Miriam Ladu, Ornella Spagnolello, Irene Comisso
items.title_zh: 成人急性护理中的高流量鼻导管氧疗：机制与临床证据
items.summary_zh: 高流量鼻导管（HFNC）氧疗广泛应用于急救、重症监护、围手术期及操作环境，但常被误解为非侵入性正压通气（NIPPV）。HFNC是一种开放式高流量氧气系统，其主要效果源于死腔清除、吸入氧分数（FiO₂）稳定性提高、加热湿化、患者舒适度，以及仅有的适度流量依赖性正气道压力。HFNC的开放接口还便于进食、饮水、说话和分泌物清除。临床证据支持HFNC主要用于急性低氧血症呼吸衰竭的特定患者，能减少与常规氧疗相比的插管率。然而，在高碳酸血症呼吸衰竭、心源性肺水肿、免疫抑制患者、肥胖及需要显著压力支持或通气卸载的环境中，证据则较为异质。当控制正压、肺泡招募或通气辅助为治疗核心时，NIPPV或持续正压通气仍为更优选择。因此，HFNC应视为优化的高流量氧疗，而非“通过鼻导管的非侵入性通气”。认识到这一区别有助于改善患者选择和治疗方案的调整。

items.title: Five Novel Sonographic Signs
items.abstract: Ultrasound is a widely used imaging modality in clinical practice, and sonographic signs serve as valuable teaching tools that aid in pattern recognition and diagnosis. This review consolidates five novel sonographic signs previously proposed by the author, including the Cracked Earth Sign for subcutaneous edema, the Mushroom Cap Sign for localized gallbladder adenomyomatosis, the LTS Sign for dilated cardiomyopathy, the LTI Sign for endocardial fibroelastosis, and the Three Pipes Sign for the suprasternal long-axis view of the aortic arch, spanning the fields of superficial ultrasound, abdominal ultrasound, and echocardiography. For each sign, its naming logic, definition, clinical implications, and teaching value are described. This review aims to facilitate a better understanding of these signs and to promote their use as teaching aids in ultrasound education.
items.authors: Xiang Ji

items.title: Large-Language Models as a Cognitive Virus
items.abstract: Large-language models (LLMs) are rapidly becoming part of human culture, reshaping how information is produced, transmitted, and used. Here we propose that their diffusion can be understood through a viral analogy, with LLM use spreading through populations, becoming embedded in cognitive and cultural practices. We model transitions among uncoupled, coupled, and persistently dependent users, and show that the interplay between social transmission, recovery, and collective reinforcement can generate tipping points and technological lock-in. A central consequence is the possibility of runaway dynamics: once a critical threshold is crossed, small increases in adoption can trigger rapid population-level shifts toward persistent dependence, with abrupt losses in cognitive competence. The same framework, however, identifies conditions for cognitive immunization, based on reducing transmission and facilitating reversibility. Our results highlight how LLM adoption may involve nonlinear collective transitions with important consequences for cognitive autonomy.
items.authors: Ricard Sole, Giulio Ruffini, Farncesca Castaldo, Marco Tuccio, Luis F. Seoane, Manlio de Domenico

items.title: Sustainable Decision-Making Framework for Hybrid Organisations: An AHP-AI-Based Approach
items.abstract: We propose a decision-making framework, methodologically based on the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), designed specifically for hybrid organizations whose activities are project-based. We adapt the AHP (a multi-criteria decision-making model) to the context of decision-making in hybrid organizations by including a preliminary screening stages (project identification and economic assessment) that ensures the financial viability of candidate projects. We also use artificial intelligence to improve the methodological robustness of the decision-making process. Our methodological adaptation of the AHP facilitates complex decision-making processes in hybrid organizations by enabling simultaneous analyses of multiple objectives and criteria and by using artificial intelligence to operationalize the AHP-based decision-making process, making the method accessible to most hybrid organizations, regardless of size. Although the proposed AHP-based method is solidly grounded in theory, the robustness and accuracy of its results ultimately depend on the quality of the information used, and the inclusion of biased or incomplete information may compromise the validity of the final ranking of alternatives. Our proposal contributes to the professionalization of decision-making in hybrid organizations, reduces reliance on intuitive approaches, enables all relevant information to be considered, and mitigates any possible biases of decision-makers.
items.authors: J. David Cabedo, Iluminada Fuertes-Fuertes, José Miguel Tirado-Beltran

items.title: From Infant Protection to Healthy Respiratory Aging: Potential Long-Term Benefits of RSV Prevention in Latin America and the Caribbean
items.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a leading cause of infant lower respiratory tract infection, hospitalization, and death in Latin America and the Caribbean, where unequal access to diagnosis, medical care, oxygen, referral, and intensive care worsens outcomes. New passive immunization tools, maternal RSV prefusion F vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies, can protect infants before peak vulnerability. Still, their population impact depends on timing, coverage, equity, financing, surveillance, and program design. Emerging regional experience with hybrid strategies may help close protection gaps among infants missed or insufficiently protected by maternal immunization. Severe early-life RSV disease is consistently associated with recurrent lower respiratory tract infections, wheezing, asthma, impaired lung-function trajectories, and increased health-care use. However, causality and long-term effects of current preventive products remain uncertain. A regional agenda linking maternal-infant cohorts, surveillance, equity analyses, and life-course economic evaluation is needed to define the full public health value of RSV prevention.
items.authors: Roberto Debbag, María L. Ávila-Agüero, José Brea, Renato de Ávila Kfouri, Flor M. Muñoz, Paula Couto

items.title: Leptin Resistance and Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress: ER Proteostasis as a Proposed Convergence Node—A Mechanistic Synthesis of Preclinical Evidence
items.abstract: Most existing reviews treat endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress as one mechanism among several in leptin resistance. This review advances a different claim: ER proteostasis may act as a central convergence node, translating metabolic, inflammatory, developmental, and nutrient-derived signals into a shared effector signature. In common obesity, leptin responsiveness is blunted despite hyperleptinaemia—the principal obstacle to leptin-based therapy. Leptin resistance is examined at the intersection of intracellular signalling networks (JAK2/STAT3, PI3K/Akt, MAPK, AMPK, mTOR, FoxO1, SOCS3, PTP1B) and hypothalamic ER stress and the unfolded protein response (UPR). This narrative synthesis incorporates 22 primary studies, with PRISMA 2020 principles used to document study selection transparently. The ER shapes leptin signalling at three levels: receptor biogenesis (SEL1L–HRD1 ERAD), receptor bioavailability (CHOP-mediated soluble receptor), and post-receptor inhibition (SOCS3/PTP1B). Distinct stressors converge on a narrow effector set (CHOP, SOCS3, PTP1B), and receptor quality control can operate independently of ER stress, demonstrating that the ER #039;s role is not confined to a stress response. The framework yields three testable hypotheses with an explicit falsification criterion, and proposes that leptin resistance comprises phenotypically distinct subtypes. The evidence base is entirely preclinical (17 rodent in vivo; 5 in vitro studies); translation to humans remains untested.
items.authors: Sule Arslan, Nida Yıldız, Halit Tanju Besler

items.title: MindCare+: A Digital Phenotyping Framework for Mental Health Monitoring and Support in Indonesia
items.abstract: Background: Indonesia has a substantial adolescent mental-health burden and a persistent service gap. The Indonesia-National Adolescent Mental Health Survey estimated that 34.9% of adolescents had a mental-health problem and 5.5% met criteria for a mental disorder in the previous 12 months, while only 2.6% of adolescents with a mental-health problem had accessed support or counselling [1,2]. Digital phenotyping may add longitudinal behavioral and physiological context, but evidence available through 2026 remains heterogeneous, methodologically fragmented, and insufficient to support autonomous psychiatric inference [4 ,6–14]. Objective: To refine the original MindCare+ student innovation concept into an evidence-bounded, human-supervised research architecture for longitudinal mental-health risk monitoring and support navigation in Indonesia, while explicitly incorporating 2025–2026 evidence on youth sensing, implementation, psychometrics, consent, and governance. Methods: We used an evidence-informed conceptual framework-development approach rather than a systematic review. The original proposal was decomposed into sensing, measurement validity, interpretation, screening, support, professional integration, governance, and implementation domains. A targeted evidence update through 15 September 2026 prioritized systematic reviews, meta-analyses, major implementation syntheses, youth-specific ethics and co-design literature, Indonesian psychometric studies, and current Indonesian regulatory or innovation pathways. Proposed functions were classified as near-term capabilities, translational hypotheses, or functions that should not be assumed without prospective validation. Results: MindCare+ is specified as a consent-based closed loop linking smartphone-derived behavioral features, optional wearable physiology, active validated self-report, privacy and data-quality gating, longitudinal personal baselines, contextual multimodal interpretation, visible uncertainty, stepped support, and human escalation. Passive signals are treated as risk-relevant context rather than psychiatric labels. The 2026 adolescent meta-analysis, which found a small overall association between passive smartphone sensing and mental-health outcomes across 45 samples (N=2939), reinforces the need to use such signals as complementary rather than determinative evidence [12]. An evidence-gated pathway is proposed from data-capture reliability and psychometric localization through prospective clinical comparison, human-factors testing, fairness and privacy evaluation, and controlled implementation. Conclusions: MindCare+ should be evaluated as a research and care-navigation architecture rather than an autonomous mental-health detector. Its central testable question is whether the smallest acceptable set of privacy-preserving longitudinal measurements, combined with context-sensitive active assessment and meaningful human oversight, can improve recognition of clinically relevant change and access to appropriate support without producing unacceptable false alerts, surveillance burden, inequity, or harm.
items.authors: Majdi Ilaf Faradis, Paramitha Dwi Fahrani, Akhmad Kholid, Ahmad Daud Fairuz, Sabrina Mutia Hafid, Qorry Amanda

items.title: Modular and Low Cost Multi-Channel Capacitive Sensing Bands Integrated with OpenCap for Gait Monitoring
items.abstract: Continuous gait monitoring is essential for clinical rehabilitation, yet traditional analysis systems are often confined to a laboratory and costly. This study develops a modular, low cost, multi-channel wearable capacitive sensing band for lower limb monitoring and as potential platform for rehabilitation research. The system utilizes repositionable conductive fabric electrodes on adjustable bands for the shank and thigh, employing an RC timing circuit to detect muscle deformation during walking and measure the capacitance via Wi-Fi for real time monitoring. Sensor characterization demonstrated high stability, with linearity exceeding 0.98, creep under 0.4%, and hysteresis below 3%, regardless of sensor conditions (Pristine, Aged, and Used). Moreover, comparison with OpenCap kinematics during normal walk across different gait phases showed strong to very strong waveform similarities with correlations exceeding 0.999 during terminal stance. Furthermore, the system demonstrated feasibility in identifying simulated hemiplegic, spastic, and Parkinsonian gait against normal walking, with abnormality thresholds reaching 40 % of the gait cycle points exceeding the abnormality threshold of |z| gt;2. These findings suggest the proposed modular system is an effective tool for identifying muscle deformation in lower limb, which is essential in gait assessment in clinical rehabilitation. Future studies should validate the device with actual patients with musculoskeletal disorders.
items.authors: Cachey Girly G. Alipala, Sybil S. Encinares, Christine Joy G. Aban, Noel Lito B. Sayson, Naomi T. Paylaga, Aljo Clair P. Pingal

items.title: Terminal Compatibility and Admissibility of a Meridional Caputo Flow Rule in Transformed-Stress Clay Plasticity
items.abstract: A clay flow rule governs contraction or dilation during plastic shearing. A fractional replacement must preserve the zero-dilatancy critical state and remain compatible with elasticity and hardening. We examine these requirements for a terminal-directed Caputo operator on a teardrop surface. The operator integrates surface slopes over a logarithmic stress interval, not elapsed loading history. Analytical derivations and incremental tests separate terminal compatibility, operator composition, stress-path identifiability and admissibility. The operator zero matches the non-associated base-model critical state only if Ω = Ψ. For kaolin, the alternative zero raises the normally consolidated undrained terminal mean stress by 18.6%. An exact identity shows why the flow candidates share the same normally consolidated stress locus yet progress differently in a numerical coordinate. Mean-stress preservation permits exact scalar composition with the SMP transformation but supplies no physical strain mapping. Two direct overconsolidated substitutions expose distinct deficiencies: coupling the loading modulus to the fractional dilatancy (F2) reverses its sign above OCR=exp(1/Ψ), whereas retaining the inherited loading modulus (F1) causes hardening inconsistency, low-OCR surface drift or negative assigned work at high OCR. These results define requirements a fractional clay formulation must satisfy before stress and strain data can test its predictions.
items.authors: Nopanom Kaewhanam, Thammanun Chatwong, Apichit Kampala, Sitthiphat Eua-apiwatch, Sivarit Sultornsanee

items.title: Antimicrobial Stewardship and One Health Perspectives: A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Background. Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a significant global health challenge, threatening the effectiveness of life-saving antimicrobial therapies, and requires a multifaceted approach for its mitigation. Methods. This article explores the One Health (OH) framework as a comprehensive strategy that integrates human, animal, and environmental health to combat AMR. Key aspects of antimicrobial stewardship across various sectors are analyzed, including hospital-based interventions, community initiatives, and veterinary practices. Environmental contributors, including antibiotic water and soil contamination, are addressed through mitigation strategies, such as advanced waste management technologies and sustainable agricultural practices. Wildlife's role in transmitting resistance is discussed, emphasizing the need for conservation efforts and environmental monitoring. This paper also reviews global success stories and collaborative programs, in Africa, Europe, and North America, illustrating the importance of integrated surveillance and policy harmonization. Results. Challenges to implementing the OH strategy, including regulatory discrepancies, communication barriers, and cultural resistance, are acknowledged. However, opportunities for progress, such as global partnerships, interdisciplinary education, and innovation, offer hope for mitigating AMR. The role of technological innovations, such as artificial intelligence, advanced data analysis, and cutting-edge antibiotic research, is explored, alongside the importance of vaccines in preventing infections with resistant pathogens. Conclusions. By fostering collaboration, promoting sustainable practices, and leveraging advanced technologies, the OH framework provides a pathway to address AMR and safeguard public, animal, and environmental health for future generations.
items.authors: Fatma Amer, Souha Kanj, Maya Dagher, Wassim Ayoubi, Mamoon A Aldeyab, J. Scott Weese

items.title: Oxford Nanopore-Based Genomic Characterization of Macrolide Resistance in Clinical em Streptococcus pyogenes /em Isolates
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A Streptococcus, GAS) remains a major human pathogen. This study aimed to determine the phenotypic profiles of macrolide resistance in S. pyogenes isolates from southeastern Turkey and to investigate underlying genotypic mechanisms using Oxford Nanopore sequencing. Methods: A total of 83 clinical isolates of S. pyogenes were collected between January 2024 and June 2025. Antimicrobial susceptibility was assessed by disk diffusion following EUCAST guidelines. Macrolide resistance phenotypes (iMLSB, cMLSB, M) were determined by the D‑zone test. Whole‑genome sequencing of erythromycin‑resistant isolates was performed using Oxford Nanopore technology, and resistance determinants were analyzed with the CARD/RGI pipeline.Results: All isolates were susceptible to penicillin. Six isolates (7.2%) exhibited erythromycin resistance: three iMLSB, two cMLSB, and one M phenotype. Adult isolates were exclusively iMLSB, whereas pediatric isolates included one M and two cMLSB phenotypes. Genotypic analysis revealed erm(A) in all iMLSB isolates, mef(A)/msr(D) in the M phenotype, and absence of major resistance genes in cMLSB isolates, which instead carried chromosomal lmrP and mef(E)‑like sequences. Co‑occurrence of tetracycline resistance genes (tetM/O) was observed in several isolates.Conclusions: Penicillin remains the cornerstone of GAS therapy; however, macrolide resistance persists through diverse mechanisms. The coexistence of erm(A)‑mediated iMLSB, mef(A)/msr(D)‑associated M phenotype, and unexplained cMLSB resistance highlights the need for routine D‑testing and genomic surveillance. These findings emphasize the importance of integrating phenotypic and genotypic approaches to monitor resistance evolution in GAS.
items.authors: Serkan Kaydaş, Asuman Akar, Ayla Behnejad Kazancık, Nida Özcan

items.title: Negentropic Value Currency: A Research Program for Re-Anchoring Monetary Value in Net Order Creation
items.abstract: The absence of a monetary value anchor independent of discretionary issuance remains an unresolved problem of monetary theory. This paper develops a conditional research program: granted the normative premise that civilizational survival is a lexicographically prior meta-constraint, the value anchor can migrate from scarcity to net order creation. We construct the negentropic theory of value, in which value is the net increment of systemic order, and civilization utility theory, in which continuous negentropic creation pursues the mastery of cosmic truth as its ultimate directional goal. The value equation Wτ = k·Eτa·Tτb·Iτc is posited rather than derived from physics; its benchmark case Wτ = √(Eτ·Tτ·Iτ) combines exergy input, non-equilibrium maintenance time, and structural information gain. Existence and uniqueness of the incentive-compatible configuration are established under stated assumptions, including quasi-linear utility, and a second-order welfare-loss bound is derived for calibration errors in the consensus coefficients α. A three-period overlapping-generations model, a general equilibrium with endogenous α (with scenario analysis when assumptions fail), mechanism defenses, and a four-layer measurement blueprint (CRN, a forward-looking research program rather than a presently deployable system) complete the program. Component-level cross-country evidence shows that R amp;D intensity alone explains 79% of the variance in innovation-output density. H1 provides executed component-level correlational evidence; H2–H5 are designed but not yet executed; the macrostability of a scarcity-free anchor is identified as the central open problem.
items.authors: Dian Cheng, Jinjun Cheng

items.title: Neonatal Anaemia in Preterm Infants: Beyond Haemoglobin - Fetal Haemoglobin, Reticulocytes and Individualised Transfusion Thresholds
items.abstract: Anaemia is almost universal during the neonatal course of extremely preterm infants and red blood cell transfusion (BT) remains one of the most frequently used treatments in neonatal intensive care. The fall in haemoglobin after preterm birth reflects developmental physiology compounded by shortened RBC survival, impaired erythropoietin response, rapid somatic growth, iron availability and iatrogenic blood loss. Although haemoglobin (Hb) concentration remains the principal laboratory measure used to guide transfusion, it provides an incomplete assessment of oxygen delivery and erythropoietic reserve. Recent evidence has therefore renewed interest in complementary measures including fetal haemoglobin (HbF), absolute reticulocyte count and reticulocyte haemoglobin content. High risk infants such as those with fetal growth restriction (FGR) may represent a distinct haematological phenotype because chronic placental insufficiency alters fetal erythropoiesis and iron utilisation before birth. Large randomised trials and a subsequent international guideline now support restrictive haemoglobin-based transfusion thresholds in very preterm infants, but substantial variation in practice persists. Furthermore, transfusion with adult donor RBCs changes more than haemoglobin concentration: it replaces HbF-rich neonatal cells with HbA-rich adult cells, altering oxygen affinity and endogenous erythropoiesis. This narrative review examines the developmental physiology and contemporary management of neonatal anaemia, with particular focus on HbF, reticulocyte parameters, FGR, transfusion thresholds and emerging approaches to individualised transfusion. Future strategies should move beyond haemoglobin concentration alone towards integration of haematological and physiological markers of oxygen delivery.
items.authors: Ceri Murphy, Jayanta Banerjee, Narendra Aladangady

items.title: Securing Local-Area Networks in AI Supercomputing Data Centers
items.abstract: Artificial-intelligence supercomputers concentrate high-value training data, model weights, credentials, accelerators, and orchestration services behind extremely fast local networks. Their security problem differs from that of a conventional office LAN because several fabrics coexist: out-of-band management, in-band services, storage, and high-performance compute communication. This survey synthesizes standards, government guidance, vendor reference architectures, and peer-reviewed systems-security research to examine how those fabrics change the attack surface. The review finds that segmentation, zero-trust access, strong device and workload identity, encrypted management, secure firmware, and independent recovery paths form a consistent baseline. However, high-performance mechanisms such as InfiniBand and Remote Direct Memory Access create residual risks because isolation identifiers are not necessarily cryptographic protections, one-sided operations can bypass host processing, and monitoring at accelerator-fabric rates is difficult. The paper proposes a cross-plane control model that binds job identity to network authorization and data provenance, then identifies research priorities in line-rate cryptography, revocable RDMA capabilities, DPU assurance, AI-aware telemetry, and disruption-tolerant containment. The resulting view treats LAN security as a property of the complete AI workload lifecycle rather than as a perimeter firewall problem.
items.authors: Manikanta Nagulapalli

items.title: Evaluability of Public Financial Support in a Climate-Exposed Livestock System: Budget Execution and Concessional Credit Allocation in Mongolia
items.abstract: Public financial support can be rapidly disbursed yet remain unevaluable when fiscal, beneficiary, exposure, and outcome records are not linked. This study audits Mongolia’s livestock-sector support using budget-execution and livestock-loss data for 2010–2024, along with aggregated records for 289 classified White Gold concessional-loan applications as of 20 June 2025. The analysis distinguishes implementation, delivery conversion, concentration, spatial traceability, and the evidentiary requirements for causal effectiveness. Support execution rose from MNT 10.9 billion in 2010 to MNT 316.1 billion in 2024; the mean execution rate was 87.55% and the minimum 45.62%. Livestock mortality was episodic, with 10.2 million losses in 2010 and 9.3 million in 2024, but aggregate fiscal data cannot separate prevention, compensation, or anticipatory financing. Of the classified applications, 145 were approved and 133 disbursed; MNT 411.4 billion was recorded as disbursed, equal to 90.8% of the approved value and 47.2% of the requested value. Disbursement was concentrated in working capital (81.4%), cashmere-related purposes (80.9%), Ulaanbaatar-registered firms (95.0%), and five banks (94.7%; HHI = 0.246). The program is measurable for implementation and concentration, but not for final regional incidence or causal effectiveness. Evaluation-ready policy requires province-level exposure, supplier and beneficiary tracing, and post-finance outcomes.
items.authors: Uyanga Gantumur

items.title: CD-KLM: A Secure Storage Architecture for Agricultural Big Data
items.abstract: With the development of smart agriculture, agricultural big data typically exhibit characteristics such as long-term accumulation and multi-source heterogeneity, which place higher demands on secure storage and sustained decryptability in long-running environments. To address this issue, this paper proposes CD-KLM, a secure storage architecture for Hadoop-based agricultural big data platforms. Specifically, we adopt a client-driven, server-lightweight-collaborative design, in which the reading and decryption capabilities of historical files are independently controlled by the client, while the server only issues collaborative salt values to authenticated clients during new-file creation. On this basis, a dynamic working-key derivation mechanism is designed based on HKDF and file-related contextual information, so that working keys no longer need to be persistently stored over the long term, thereby reducing the risk of malicious data decryption caused by prolonged exposure of critical key material. Meanwhile, threshold-based key recovery is unified at the root-key level, enabling the system to restore its overall decryption capability even when critical keys are damaged or lost. Experimental results in a Hadoop distributed environment show that, while ensuring key recoverability and continuous decryptability, the proposed architecture imposes only a low impact on system throughput, making it suitable for long-running secure storage scenarios for agricultural big data.
items.authors: Bochun Cao, Hanbing Deng, Yuncheng Zhou, Teng Miao

items.title: Bousfield Reachability on Generalized Pentagons
items.abstract: Martínez Alberga and Roitzheim ([5], Theorem 5.4) proved that every model structure on the fivepoint pentagon can be obtained from the trivial model by left and right Bousfield localizations. We extend this result to generalized pentagons with an arbitrarily long second branch. Non-universal models are constructed by extending model structures along full inclusions of chain categories. For universal models, a functor to the category 0 → 1, or its dual, identifies a predecessor with one acyclic class unchanged. A factorization argument describes its weak equivalences as the arrows sent to identities. The resulting construction proves reachability for the whole family. The proof establishes existence of a finite localization sequence, without an optimal bound on its length.
items.authors: Ramiro Ramirez

items.title: Knowledge-Guided Temporal Fuzzy Learning for Interpretable Prediction of Clinical Deterioration
items.abstract: Interpretable prediction from longitudinal clinical data requires more than accurate risk estimates: a model should preserve meaningful domain structure, reveal how risk evolves over time, and remain auditable when transferred across heterogeneous healthcare settings. We address this challenge with a Knowledge-Guided Temporal Fuzzy Neural Network (KG-TFNN) that integrates clinically anchored yet trainable fuzzy states, explicit temporal fuzzy-risk and observation-process descriptors, parsimonious additive and cross-feature Sugeno inference, and attention-based temporal aggregation within a single auditable prediction pathway. Unlike approaches that rely primarily on latent representations or post-hoc explanations, KG-TFNN exposes membership evolution, feature-level risk contributions, native rule firing, temporal contributions, and parameter drift for direct structural analysis. We evaluated the framework for predicting a ≧ 2-point increase in Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score within 6 h using patient-disjoint MIMIC-IV development and locked testing, followed by fully frozen transport to the multicenter eICU-CRD database comprising 80,239 patients across 205 hospitals. Explicit temporal representation produced the largest controlled ablation effect on discrimination (ΔAUROC = 0.0510), exceeding the contribution of knowledge-guided initialization alone (ΔAUROC = 0.0061), while structural analyses demonstrated reproducible global behavior and identifiable membership and rule evolution. Although KG-TFNN did not exceed tuned LightGBM in discrimination, it enabled forms of temporal and structural auditing unavailable from predictive performance alone and revealed important limitations in cross-database calibration and patient-specific explanation. These findings establish KG-TFNN as a rigorously evaluated framework for studying the trade-off between predictive performance, semantic interpretability, temporal dynamics, and transportability, providing a reusable design principle for trustworthy longitudinal machine learning rather than a task-specific clinical alarm.
items.authors: Yan-Wei Li, David Chunhu Li

items.title: Synthetic Receptors for Specific Cell Imaging and Signal Transduction
items.abstract: Specific cell tracking or targeted modulation of cellular responses are often limited by the availability, specificity and effector functions of endogenous cell-surface receptors. Synthetic receptors with customizable functionality can overcome these limitations. Based on a qualitative survey of the literature, this narrative review describes the design, the functionality and the applications of nanobody based synthetic receptor/ligand systems that employ either GFP/mCherry or the clinically approved humanized antibody Palivizumab as ligands. Depending on their molecular architecture, these systems can mediate cargo internalization for cell tracking or induce defined cellular responses through engineered interleukin, interferon, or Fas signaling pathways. We position these platforms within the broader field of synthetic receptors by discussing engineered GPCR- and Notch-based systems and briefly outline the development and clinical application of CAR T cells to illustrate the translational potential of synthetic receptor systems. Finally, we discuss the opportunities and limitations of GFP/mCherry- and Palivizumab-based systems, with particular emphasis on immunogenicity, in vivo applicability, manufacturability, scalability, and clinical translation. By linking modular receptor design to distinct functional outputs, this review highlights both the established value of GFP/mCherry- and Palivizumab-based synthetic receptor–ligand systems as experimental tools and their potential for future applications in molecular imaging and controlled signal transduction.
items.authors: Zeynep-Büsra Tiren, Lotta Horrix, Doreen M. Floß, Sascha Malaczynski, Constantin Czekelius, Sebastian Temme

items.title: Association Between Quantitative Brushing Efficacy and Dental Caries Severity in Schoolchildren
items.abstract: Background: Although toothbrushing is widely recognized as a cornerstone of caries prevention, oral hygiene has traditionally been assessed using self-reported frequency or categorical plaque indices. Evidence regarding the relationship between objectively quantified brushing efficacy and cumulative caries severity remains limited. This study evaluated the association between a quantitative brushing efficacy index and dental caries severity among schoolchildren. Methods: A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 200 schoolchildren examined during a community dental campaign in 2025. Caries was assessed using Decayed, Missing, Filled Teeth indices following Word Health Organization criteria. Severe caries was defined as Decayed, Missing, Filled Teeth ≥5. Oral hygiene was measured using a brushing efficacy index, expressed as the percentage of biofilm removed after supervised brushing. Associations were evaluated using chi-square tests and logistic regression models adjusted for age and sex. Results: Caries prevalence was 95.5%, with a mean Decayed, Missing, Filled Teeth of 4.99 ± 2.96. Severe caries was observed in 49% of participants. No statistically significant differences were found across tertiles of brushing efficacy (χ² (2) =2.18; p=0.336). In regression analysis, each 10% increase in brushing efficacy was not significantly associated with severe caries (adjusted OR=0.92; 95% CI: 0.81–1.03; p=0.154), although a protective trend was observed. Conclusions: This population exhibited an extremely high burden of dental caries. Quantitative brushing efficacy showed a non-significant protective trend, suggesting that in high-risk contexts, caries severity is influenced by multifactorial determinants beyond isolated oral hygiene performance.
items.authors: Andrea Coello Hidalgo, Luis Chauca Bajaña, Ana Alvear Miquilena, Diego Quiguango Farias, Maria Rodriguez Tates, Byron Velasquez Ron

items.title: Multiplicative Decomposition-Embedded Logarithmic Strain-Based Statements for Viscoelasticity in Glaciological Applications
items.abstract: This paper formulates a thermodynamically consistent finite-strain Maxwell-Glen model for glaciological applications in a Lagrangian setting. A multiplicative decomposition of the deformation gradient separates the elastic and viscous mappings, while a trace-free material velocity gradient describes isochoric creep. The elastic state is represented by a logarithmic strain, and its associated material stress drives a temperature-dependent Glen law. Under the isotropic constitutive assumptions, commutation reduces the multiplicative metric update to an additive elastic-viscous corrector. The exponential map is evaluated by a Cayley-Hamilton reduction for generally nonsymmetric arguments, and a consistent linearisation supplies the material tangent. Homogeneous simple shear verifies agreement with spatial Glen flow under non-coaxial deformation. A self-weighted plane-strain column confirms preservation of the incremental viscous Jacobian to the solver tolerance. For a floating shelf, depth-dependent viscous resistance reverses the shelf-edge bending relative to uniform viscosity.
items.authors: Paul Namalomba, Sebastian Skatulla, Carlo Sansour, Maxime Nutte, Michael Kaliske

items.title: The Spiral Structure Model: A Geometric Phenomenology of Wave-Particle Duality, Spin, and Electromagnetic Coupling
items.abstract: The Spiral Structure Model (SSM) is a phenomenological model in Bohr’s tradition: restricted to kinematics and geometry, it trades dynamical depth for ontological clarity and experimental exposure. Three postulates suffice: (I) the photon is a pointlike energy quantum in uniform helical motion, axial and circulation speeds both equal to c; (II) physical space is an elastic, relativistically covariant medium sustaining vortex excitations; (III) the electron is a stable topological vortex defect of that medium. These yield, every step labeled: the photon’s circulation angular momentum mcrγ = ℏ as a consistency theorem identified with its spin; logarithmic vortex confinement with zero free parameters; the two polarization states and no longitudinal mode; orbital angular momentum as an ensemble property; the electron’s 720-degree periodicity and spin ℏ/2 from π1(SO(3)) = Z2; the fine-structure constant as a ratio of structural scales; the free radiation field as an ensemble statistical moment; a phase-coupling account of two-slit interference; and a double-helix ontology of entangled pairs reproducing the CHSH value 2√2. Three falsifiable discriminants are stated with kill criteria: a wavelength-locked on-axis detection void, a spin-dependent electron form-factor window near Q = mc, and a circulation-periodic component in entangled-pair coincidence timing.
items.authors: Jinjun Cheng, Dian Cheng

items.title: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control-Based Reverse Path-Planning and Path-Tracking Control of a Vehicle with Trailer System
items.abstract: Reverse parking of a vehicle with trailer is a challenging task to complete for human drivers due to its articulated structure, unstable reverse-motion behaviors and unintuitive steering responses. This paper proposes a compact, trailer-centric nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC)-based automation routine that integrates local motion generation and feedback control into a single receding-horizon framework, without requiring a separately planned reference path or a dedicated path-tracking controller. The trailer unit is represented as a virtual standalone vehicle, and its motion requirements are mapped to the vehicle unit inputs via inverse kinematics. This allows trajectory prediction and tracking objective to be represented only with trailer states, hence reducing the dimensions of the horizon-stacked state and weighting matrices compared to using the full vehicle-trailer formulation. The proposed controller is implemented as a single-shooting nonlinear program (NLP) and supports a three-staged maneuver sequence to obtain an improved final parking configuration. Simulation results demonstrate successful vehicle-trailer parking maneuvers, while hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) results further illustrate that online NMPC computation times can remain within the real-time sampling deadline, indicating that the proposed NMPC framework can offer a practical receding-horizon automation routine for vehicle-trailer reverse parking tasks.
items.authors: Xincheng Cao, Haochong Chen, Bilin Aksun-Guvenc, Levent Guvenc, Brian Link, Peter J Richmond

items.title: On-Scene Time-Dependent Probability of a Favorable Neurological Outcome in Cases of Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest with an Initial Shockable Rhythm: A Retrospective Study Using the National Utstein Data in Japan
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is a major public health issue. During on-scene resuscitation, emergency medical services (EMS) must balance continued resuscitation against early transport for advanced in-hospital treatment. We aimed to examine the time-dependent probabilities at the scene for favorable neurological outcomes of OHCA with an initial shockable rhythm. Methods: We conducted a retrospective study using a dataset that combined the Japanese national Utstein data and emergency transport data. Of the OHCA cases recorded between January 2017 to December 2022, 22,383 with an initial shockable rhythm were included. We examined the time-dependent probabilities of achieving return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) with a favorable neurological outcome at each minute of on-scene time. Results: On-scene ROSC was achieved in 5,095 cases, and favorable neurological outcomes at 1 month were obtained in 3,182 cases. The probability of achieving on-scene ROSC fell below 10% after 10 min from EMS contact and decreased to ≤5% after 20 min. Among patients who achieved on-scene ROSC, the time-dependent probabilities of a favorable neurological outcome appeared similar according to sex, witness status, and bystander CPR, whereas patients aged lt; 75 years maintained higher probabilities than those aged ≥75 years. Conclusions: Under current resuscitation practices in Japan, the probability of achieving on-scene ROSC in patients with OHCA and an initial shockable rhythm fell below 10% after 10 min from EMS contact and decreased to ≤5% after 20 min. Patients aged lt; 75 years may remain candidates for prolonged on-scene resuscitation, regardless of witness status or bystander CPR.
items.authors: Keita Miyazaki, Arisa Kinoshita, Koji Yamamoto, Keisuke Tsuruta, Hideki Asai, Yasuyuki Kawai

items.title: Domain Adaptation and Annotation Efficiency in Remote-Sensing LULC Mapping: A Systematic Review of Active Learning and Vision–Language Models and a Conceptual Framework for the Brazilian Cerrado
items.abstract: Accurate and transferable land-use and land-cover (LULC) mapping in the Brazilian Cerrado is challenged by spatial and temporal heterogeneity, domain shift, and the high cost of expert annotation. This systematic review with qualitative methodological synthesizes evidence on Active Learning (AL), domain adaptation, remote-sensing foundation models, and Remote-Sensing Vision–Language Models (RS-VLMs), focusing on their complementary roles in annotation-efficient and transferable LULC mapping. Evidence was synthesized qualitatively because the reviewed studies differed substantially in sensors, tasks, datasets, domain-shift conditions, and evaluation protocols. The literature indicates that uncertainty-, diversity-, and representativeness-based AL can improve annotation efficiency, while foundation models and RS-VLMs provide increasingly transferable representations and few-shot or open-vocabulary capabilities across remote-sensing applications. However, direct empirical evidence integrating transferable representations, AL, and domain adaptation for Cerrado LULC monitoring remains limited. Based on the convergence of these evidence streams, we propose a conceptual human-in-the-loop framework that combines transferable representations with selective target-domain annotation and subsequent adaptation. The framework is hypothesis-driven rather than experimentally validated. The review identifies priorities for empirical evaluation, including multimodal benchmarks, standardized AL protocols, spatially and temporally independent validation, explainability, and continuous human-in-the-loop adaptation. This synthesis provides a methodological basis for future domain-adaptive LULC monitoring in the Brazilian Cerrado.
items.authors: Daniel Soares, Edilson Bias, Li Weigang, Pedro Brom, Helci Ramos

items.title: Classical vs. AI-Based Methods in Autonomous Vehicles: Reproducible Experiments from Perception to Field Safety Data
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is used throughout autonomous vehicle (AV) software, yet published comparisons of perception, estimation, prediction, planning and control methods rarely share data, protocols or statistical analysis, which makes their trade-offs difficult to judge. This paper reports a reproducible experimental evaluation that spans the AV stack under a single protocol: fixed seeds, held-out test data, validation-based tuning, 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and paired non-parametric tests with multiplicity correction. Twelve experiments address four research questions using the public comma10k driving dataset, seeded simulations, and public field data. On 150 held-out real frames, context features raise drivable-area intersection over union (IoU) from 0.701 to 0.803 (p lt; 10−11), whereas a classical lane detector reaches an F1 score of 0.658 [0.620, 0.694] irrespective of frame brightness (p = 0.93). Odometry–GNSS fusion reduces outage error from 265.5 m to 30.2 m. Multimodal prediction halves displacement error only because it outputs several hypotheses; its single-hypothesis variant is the worst model. Q-learning reduces lane-change crash rate from 59.8%to 6.3% relative to a rule with identical inputs, and validation-tuned controllers reverse the rankings obtained with hand-picked gains. FedAvg recovers 54–74% of the accuracy gap between isolated and centralised training. A re-analysis of 220.6 million rider-only miles of Waymo data confirms an 83%reduction in injury crashes (ratio 0.170 [0.143, 0.201]), while about 388 million miles would be needed to demonstrate an 80% fatality reduction. All code and data are released.
items.authors: Ajay Waghmare, Subramaniam Ganesan

items.title: Comparing Linear Mixed Models, Generalized Estimating Equations, and Generalized Linear Mixed Models Under Monotone Missing-at-Random Dropout in Longitudinal Clinical Trials: A Monte Carlo Simulation Study
items.abstract: Background: Longitudinal clinical trials are often affected by dropout, which can influence statistical inference if not handled appropriately. This simulation study examined three widely used approaches for analyzing repeated measurements under monotone missing-at-random dropout: linear mixed-effects models (LME), generalized estimating equations (GEE), and generalized linear mixed models (GLMM). Methods: A factorial Monte Carlo design generated longitudinal datasets defined by patient, visit, and treatment group. Simulations included a continuous and a binary outcome under two effect-size scenarios, three sample sizes (100, 200, 500), and four dropout rates (10% to 40%), with 1000 replications per design cell. Gaussian LME and GEE were fitted to the continuous outcome; logistic GLMM and GEE to the binary outcome. Results: All four methods produced small, stable bias across the full design, and RMSE decreased with larger samples. Coverage of the nominal 95% interval stayed close to target, from about 93% to 96%, while Type I error remained near nominal. Power declined with dropout but exceeded 99% at N=500. Both GEE models converged in every replication; logistic GLMM converged less consistently, between 96% and 99%. The clearest difference concerned standard errors: robust sandwich estimates agreed closely with empirical variability, whereas naive model-based estimates, particularly for Gaussian GEE, consistently underestimated it. Conclusion: Under monotone missing-at-random dropout, reliable GEE inference depended on the robust sandwich variance estimator rather than the naive alternative. Comparisons between GLMM and GEE were meaningful only when each method was evaluated against its own estimand, conditional for GLMM and marginal for GEE.
items.authors: Najmeh Jabbari

items.title: A Fast Operator-Interpolation Mapped Spectral Method for Variable-Order Fractional PDEs
items.abstract: We propose a fast mapped spectral method for a class of variable-order fractional partial differential equations posed on the real line. The main difficulty arises from the spatially dependent fractional order of the operator, which prevents the direct diagonalisation techniques available for constant-order fractional Laplacians and leads, in general, to expensive nonlocal discretisations. To overcome this limitation, we introduce an operator-interpolation strategy in which the variable-order fractional Laplacian is approximated by a finite combination of constant-order fractional operators evaluated at suitably chosen interpolation nodes in the fractional-order variable. Each constant-order contribution is treated through a Fourier-like mapped Chebyshev representation on R, allowing the corresponding nonlocal operator to be evaluated efficiently in spectral space. Chebyshev interpolation with respect to the fractional order is employed to obtain an accurate approximation over a prescribed interval s(x) ∈ [smin, smax].
